newsitem.title: USA: U.S. court rules takeover costs deductible - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: U.S. court rules takeover costs deductible - WSJ.

text.p: The ruling of a federal appeals court in Chicago, saying costs companies incur battling takeovers are tax deductible as ordinary business expenses should stiffen the resolve of those fighting the Internal Revenue Service over tax bills in similar cases, The Wall Street Journal said.
In Thursday's electronic edition, the paper quoted a lawyer saying the decision "should have an immediate and important effect" on many companies.
The case involved a predecessor of food-sweetener concern A.E. Staley Manufacturing Co, the article said.
Nearly a decade ago Staley enlisted investment bankers to help resist a takeover bid by Tate & Lyle Plc, the article said.
Staley succumbed to the bid after paying more than $12.5 million to First Boston and Merrill Lynch, the article said.
The IRS argued that the fees Staley paid represented non-deductible capital expenditures because the IRS believed those expenses produced long-term benefits, the article said.
The Seventh U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals last week said that because the investment bankers failed to ward off the takeover, there was no long-term benefit, the story said.
